contexts.text: Truths of faith are like rays of light; love being the flame.

From the modification of the inflowing rays of light, colours come forth... In spiritual things... the blackness is the proprium, which absorbs and extinguishes the rays of light; but the whiteness is the truth and good which man supposes he does from himself, which reflects and rejects the rays of light. The rays of light which fall upon these, and as it were modify them, are from the Lord... for the rays of spiritual light are from no other source.
Rays of golden flame for those in affections of good; and rays of silver light for those in affections of truth.
Every colour consists of innumerable rays; so that myriads constitute one General which is perceptible. AC 1623:end.
His hatred and its filth are the recipients of the rays of good and truth from the Lord, which rays of good and truth they turn into fire, smoke, and thick darkness.
The rays of the internal sight are ideas.
The goods in the natural man receive the heat of the light of Heaven; and the truth its rays, that is, faith.
The things which in the light of the world make one ray, in the light of Heaven make myriads...
Light inflows from Heaven... and causes the reasons which he sees with the understanding to be so many rays of that light.
The radiant circle around the head, represented the Divine from Him... AC 9407:14.
They concentrate the influx of happiness from Heaven upon themselves, and do not transmit it to others; and are like objects which do not remit, but absorb, the rays of light.
This is as it is with the objects of sight, from which there diffuses itself a sphere of rays to a great distance, which falls into man's sight... AC 6603:2.
The heat is varied according to the direct or oblique incidence of the sun's rays.
The first two successives of Divine truth are as it were radiant belts from the flaming... HH 120.
Transmits the rays of heavenly light.
A thousand enemies cannot endure one ray of the light of Heaven. DLW 254:end.
Directly in the line, or ray, in which the Angels look to the Lord.
Compared to the multitude of rays which go forth from the stars, and carry their heat and light into the earth. DLW 366:3.

Every ray of intellectual light is an image of that love from which and to which it is continued (as every ray of natural light is an image of the sun). Hence, from the perpetual rays of such a kind, there is effected a light which both illuminates and kindles the human mind.
In human minds there are rays both of light and of love: nothing is excited by the rays of light, but by the rays of love.
Represented by the sudden closing of lines, or radii.
The Spirits were found... sometimes as if by rays...
Rays like bright stings seemed to go forth from his eyes... SE 3541.
Represented by an infant surrounded by rays.
Round the head a kind of radiant circle, Ath 153.
They absorb the rays of the Lord's mercy...
Man's love is like fire, and his thoughts are like the rays of light thence...
The radiant circles are devolutions of the infinite...
4. 2. There can be no extension except by means of rays of light from wisdom, by means of heat from love; thus by means of fibres vivified, which are the rays formed.
